subject: Renewal & consolidation: GPU pool resize, temporary uplift and billing grace
messages:
From: Sophie Kramer <sophie.kramer@acme.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-20T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal: capacity questions and short-term uplift

Hi Lauren,

Quick note as we start the renewal conversation — our summer release caused a sustained uplift in inference usage and we expect another spike in Q4. We currently run two dedicated GPU pools (prod and analytics) and would like to explore consolidating them into a single pool to simplify ops and reduce headroom waste.

Two asks up front:
- Can Redwood provide a temporary uplift (3 months) above our current commit to cover expected Q4 spikes while we move to a consolidated pool?
- When consolidating, can you guarantee throughput (tokens/sec) for the new pool size so our SREs can sign off on SLAs?

We attached a usage export for May–July for reference. Also, procurement will want to understand what a short-term uplift costs and whether we can get any billing grace if the consolidation work slips past the renewal date.

Looking forward to a quick sketch of options — we need something to review with finance by next week.

Thanks,
Sophie
Sr. Platform Engineer — Acme AI

Attachment: acme_usage_report_May-Jul.csv (csv, 72KB)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Sophie Kramer <sophie.kramer@acme.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-21T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: capacity questions and short-term uplift

Hi Sophie — thanks for the usage file, that helps. High level thoughts:

1) Temporary uplift: we can offer a 3-month uplift on top of your existing reserved commit as a billable short-term buffer. Pricing: 1.35x of your committed unit rate for the uplift months (we calculate per-GPU-hour equivalent).

2) Consolidation: we can consolidate the two pools into a single pool pinned to a new reserved commit. Based on your May–July profile, a single pool sized at 160 A100-equivalent units should absorb peak load while improving utilization. We can guarantee a baseline throughput (tokens/sec) for the pinned commit; higher burst traffic would be served by configured burst capacity with a documented latency envelope.

3) Billing grace window: we can give a 2-month bill hold (no penalty) for the consolidation cutover if you sign the renewal this month and provide a mutually agreed runbook for the migration. After the grace window, standard billing resumes.

I attached a quick sketch of the pricing scenarios (consolidate + 3-month uplift vs. renew-as-is + uplift). If you’re happy, I’ll loop in Karthik and Kimberly for discount approval and a formal quote (Acme-1467).

Proposed next step: quick call tomorrow to walk through numbers? I’m available 11–12 PDT.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Acme_Renewal_Quote_v3.pdf (pdf, 48KB)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-22T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal: capacity questions and short-term uplift — approval request

Team — forwarding Acme’s ask and my proposed options. TL;DR: customer wants 3-month uplift + consolidate two pools into one 160-unit commit. They also asked for a 2-month billing grace window if consolidation slips.

Numbers (sketch):
- Current commit: 110 units
- Proposed commit: 160 units (consolidated)
- Temporary uplift (3 months): additional 40 units billed at 1.35x unit rate
- Suggested term: 12 months start on sign
- Proposed commercial: 12% net of standard list on the 12-month commit; uplift months billed at uplift rate without discount.

Asks:
- Karthik — do we have flexibility to move to 12% vs our standard 10% band for this region/segment? They are an upsell motion and will likely convert permanent uplift after Q4 usage stabilizes.
- Kimberly — can finance accommodate a 2-month billing grace on the uplift/invoicing (not a credit) if they provide a migration runbook and target cutover within 60 days?

I’ve attached the draft consolidation runbook that our solutions team put together; it has the migration steps and rollback plan.

Thanks,
Lauren

Attachment: consolidation_runbook_draft.md (md, 9KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Sophie Kramer <sophie.kramer@acme.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-23T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal & consolidation: GPU pool resize, temporary uplift and billing grace

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear ask and the usage export.

We spoke internally and can commit to the following commercial terms for Acme (deal ACME-1467):

1) Consolidated reserved commit: 160 A100-equivalent units, 12-month term.
2) Temporary uplift: +40 units for 3 months billed at 1.35x unit rate.
3) Discount: 12% off list on the 12-month reserved commit (applies to the base commit only; uplift months billed at uplift rate).
4) Throughput guarantee: we will guarantee baseline throughput per token profile documented in the attached SLAs. Bursts served by burst capacity have a latency envelope (p95 under normal conditions).
5) Billing grace: we will defer invoicing on migration-related incremental uplift charges for up to 60 days from sign (subject to an agreed migration runbook and weekly migration status updates). This is a billing deferral — not a forgiveness of charges.

Next steps: I’ve attached the updated quote and DocuSign link for signature. Once signed, we’ll schedule a migration working session with solutions and SRE to finalize the consolidation runbook and cutover window.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/Acme/Sign/ABCDEF123456
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACME-1467

Sophie — if that looks acceptable I can send the formal DocuSign now and coordinate the post-sign migration kickoff.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, North America — Redwood Inference

Attachment: Acme_Renewal_Quote_v3.pdf (pdf, updated 2026-08-23)
